name: capell-app/discovery-foundation
description: A shared list of each site's public pages, so search, 404 suggestions and other packages that read it agree on what visitors can see.

healthChecks.label: Discovery Foundation public URL contributors are registered.

marketplace.summary: Builds one list of public web addresses per site and language, leaving out hidden, restricted and search-excluded pages.
marketplace.description: A building block that other Capell packages install for you. It gathers the public web addresses of a site into one list, per site and language, so packages that read it get the same answer about what visitors can reach. Hidden pages, restricted pages and pages marked to stay out of search results are left off. It has no admin screens and nothing for editors to set up, and it works without an outside service.
marketplace.problem: My search, 404 suggestions and site checks could disagree about which pages are public.
marketplace.outcome: Every package that reads the list gets the same answer about what is public.

faq.question: Do I have to install Discovery Foundation myself?
faq.answer: No. It comes along with the packages that need it, such as Search and Site Discovery, and you never open or configure it.

faq.question: Does it give my site a sitemap or a search page?
faq.answer: No. It has no screens, settings or buttons and no sitemap or search results of its own. It only keeps the shared list of public addresses that other packages read.

faq.question: Which pages are left off the list of public addresses?
faq.answer: A published page is left off if it's hidden, set to ask search engines not to list it, or open only to signed-in visitors. Disabled sites and languages never appear.

faq.question: Does it contact an outside service or store anything of its own?
faq.answer: No. It has no outside service and no database tables of its own. It builds the list from your pages whenever another package asks for it.
